/-!
# Erdős Problem 228

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/228](https://www.erdosproblems.com/228)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos228

/--
Does there exist, for all large $n$, a polynomial $P$ of degree $n$, with coefficients $\pm1$, such
that $$\sqrt n \ll |P(z)| \ll \sqrt n$$ for all $|z|=1$, with the implied constants independent of
$z$ and $n$?

The answer is yes, proved by Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST19].

[BBMST19] Balister, P. and Bollob\'{A}s, B. and Morris, R. and Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., _Flat Littlewood Polynomials Exist_. arXiv:1907.09464 (2019).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 12 41] -- TODO(lezeau): I'm a little unhappy with the `41` tag
theorem erdos_228 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (c₁ : ℝ) (c₂ : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.degree = n ∧
    (∀ i ≤ n, p.coeff i = 1 ∨ p.coeff i = -1) ∧
    ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 →
    ( √n < c₁ * ‖p.eval z‖ ∧ ‖p.eval z‖ < c₂ * √n ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos228

reformulations.difference: The source's `√n ≪ |P(z)| ≪ √n` with absolute implied constants is written as `√n < c₁ * ‖p.eval z‖ ∧ ‖p.eval z‖ < c₂ * √n`. The constants `c₁ c₂ : ℝ` have no positivity condition, both bounds are strict, and the lower-bound constant multiplies |P(z)| rather than √n. "Polynomial of degree n with coefficients ±1" is written as `p.degree = n ∧ ∀ i ≤ n, p.coeff i = 1 ∨ p.coeff i = -1` over `ℂ[X]`, and "for all large n" as `∀ᶠ n in atTop`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The file's right-hand side is equivalent to the source form SourceForm: ∃ δ > 0, ∃ Δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n, ∃ Littlewood p of degree n, ∀ z with ‖z‖ = 1, δ√n ≤ ‖p z‖ ≤ Δ√n. (⇒) Take some n ≥ 1 in the eventual set and evaluate at z = 1. Then √n > 0 and ‖p 1‖ ≥ 0, so √n < c₁‖p 1‖ forces c₁ > 0 and ‖p 1‖ < c₂√n forces c₂ > 0. Set δ = 1/c₁ and Δ = c₂; the strict bounds give the non-strict ones. (⇐) Set c₁ = 2/δ and c₂ = 2Δ. For n ≥ 1, (2/δ)‖p z‖ ≥ 2√n > √n and ‖p z‖ ≤ Δ√n < 2Δ√n. So neither the missing sign conditions nor the strict inequalities change the claim. `p.degree = n` together with the coefficient condition describes exactly the Littlewood polynomials of degree n (the zero polynomial is excluded). I proved `LeanRHS ↔ SourceForm` in Lean (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and type-checked `Erdos228.erdos_228 : True ↔ LeanRHS` with the verbatim right-hand side.

review.notes:
The file has one declaration, `Erdos228.erdos_228`. It states the problem as posed on erdosproblems.com/228: ∃ constants, then for all large n a ±1-coefficient polynomial of degree n with √n ≪ |P(z)| ≪ √n uniformly on the unit circle. The `answer(True)` polarity is correct (the source says the answer is yes), and `research solved` matches the page status "PROVED (LEAN)". BBMST Theorem 1.1 proves the stronger "for all n ≥ 2". The Lean statement encodes the question's weaker "for all large n", which is what the source asks. A plain `∀ n` would be false, since n = 0 and n = 1 fail; I checked n = 0 in Lean.

Metadata that is not a finding:
(1) The erdosproblems.com page records a Lean-verified proof. `plby/lean-proofs` has `src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos228.lean`, whose theorem restates this exact right-hand side. The FC file has no `@[formal_proof ...]` attribute. It could get one after the checks in PROOFS.md; I did not verify that proof's axioms. The recorded status is not stale, so this is not listed as a status issue.
(2) The docstring reference spells the author as "Bollob\'{A}s" instead of "Bollob\'{a}s", and cites the 2019 arXiv preprint, while the site cites Ann. of Math. 192 (2020), 977–1004. Both are cosmetic.
(3) Erdős's original 1957 paper (users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1957-13.pdf) is a scanned image with no text layer, and no OCR was available. I relied on the erdosproblems.com text and BBMST's account of Erdős's question instead.
